ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are 10 islands in the figure, among which the island on the left is labeled A, and the island slightly right of center is labeled B. Name the unlabeled islands according to position: the upper-left is U, the upper-left-middle is C, the upper-right is T, the right-upper is R, the middle is X, the lower-left is L, the lower-middle is D, and the lower-right is E. From the figure it can be seen that the bridges include A-U, A-C, A-X, A-L, U-C, C-T, T-X, T-B, T-R, R-B, X-B, L-D, D-B, D-E, B-E, 15 bridges in total. Reasoning: From A to B, three routes that do not share bridges can be seen: A-X-B, A-L-D-B, A-C-T-B. Because these three routes have no common bridge, closing 1 bridge or 2 bridges can at most destroy 1 or 2 of the routes, and at least one path from A to B will still remain, so at least 3 bridges need to be closed. On the other hand, after closing these 3 bridges A-X, C-T, L-D, the side where A is located has only A, U, C, L connected to each other, and can no longer lead to the islands on the right side such as X, T, D, B, etc., so A and B are disconnected. Therefore at least 3 bridges need to be closed.

method.method_draft: First label the unlabeled islands by their positions in the image: upper-left U, upper-middle C, top-center T, upper-right R, center X, lower-left L, bottom-middle D, and lower-right E, in addition to A and B. Read the bridges from the image, especially the three visually separate A-to-B routes: A-X-B, A-L-D-B, and A-C-T-B. These three routes share no bridges, so closing only one or two bridges cannot block all of them. Then exhibit a set of three bridges whose closure works: close A-X, C-T, and L-D. After those are removed, the component containing A is confined to the left-side islands A, U, C, and L, while B remains on the right side. Therefore the minimum is 3.

From the image, make an adjacency list for the 10 islands: A is connected to U, C, X, and L; U to A and C; C to A, U, and T; X to A, T, and B; L to A and D; T to C, X, B, and R; R to T and B; D to L, B, and E; E to D and B; B to X, T, R, D, and E. For any proposed final A-side component S not containing B, the bridges that must be closed are exactly the edges from S to the outside. Enumerate connected choices of S containing A and count these boundary edges. The minimum boundary size occurs, for example, at S={A,U,C,L}, whose outside bridges are A-X, C-T, and L-D, giving boundary size 3. A direct check of the other connected A-containing choices gives no boundary of size 1 or 2. Hence the minimum number of bridges to close is 3.
